idea: a CLI todo app with local storage

plan.summary: A command-line todo application that stores tasks in local JSON files. Users can add, list, complete, and delete todos with a simple CLI interface.

phases.name: Project setup
steps: Initialize a Python project with a main entry point file (e.g., cli_todo.py or __main__.py)
Install Click via pip and create requirements.txt with dependencies
Create a data directory structure for storing todo JSON files

phases.name: Core data layer
steps: Create a storage module that handles reading/writing todos to a local JSON file (default location: ~/.cli_todo/todos.json)
Implement functions to load all todos from storage, and handle file creation if it doesn't exist
Add error handling for file I/O operations and invalid JSON

phases.name: CLI commands
steps: Create 'add' command: takes a todo text argument, generates a unique ID and timestamp, saves to storage
Create 'list' command: displays all todos with their IDs, text, completion status, and creation date
Create 'complete' command: takes a todo ID, marks it as done in storage
Create 'delete' command: takes a todo ID, removes it from storage
Create 'clear' command: removes all completed todos from storage

phases.name: User experience polish
steps: Add color output to list command (e.g., strikethrough or dim text for completed items)
Add confirmation prompts for destructive operations (delete, clear)
Implement --help text for all commands with clear usage examples
Add a 'stats' command showing total todos, completed count, and pending count

phases.name: Testing and documentation
steps: Create unit tests for storage module (read/write/update operations)
Create integration tests for CLI commands using Click's testing utilities
Write a README with installation instructions, usage examples for each command
Add docstrings to all functions

manual_checklist: Verify Python 3.9+ is installed on the development machine
Decide on the default todos.json storage location (home directory recommended)

idea: a CLI todo app with local storage

plan.summary: A command-line todo application that lets users add, list, complete, and delete tasks, persisting data to a local JSON file.
stack: lowdb or plain fs for JSON storage

phases.name: Project Setup
steps: Initialize a Node.js project with `npm init -y`
Install dependencies: commander, chalk, nanoid (for unique task IDs)
Install dev dependencies: jest
Set up project structure: /src/index.js (entry), /src/commands/ (add.js, list.js, done.js, remove.js, edit.js), /src/storage.js (data persistence), /src/task.js (Task model)
Configure package.json 'bin' field to make the CLI globally invokable as 'todo'
Set up .gitignore for node_modules and data files if needed

phases.name: Storage Layer
steps: Implement storage.js to read/write tasks to a JSON file located at ~/.todo-cli/tasks.json
Create function to initialize the storage file and directory if they don't exist
Implement loadTasks() and saveTasks(tasks) functions with error handling for corrupted/missing files
Define Task schema: {id, title, description (optional), completed (bool), priority (optional: low/medium/high), createdAt, completedAt}

phases.name: Core CLI Commands
steps: Set up Commander.js in index.js with program name, version, and description
Implement 'todo add <title>' command with optional flags --description, --priority
Implement 'todo list' command with optional flags --all, --completed, --pending, --priority to filter tasks; display in a formatted table using chalk for color coding by status/priority
Implement 'todo done <id>' command to mark a task as completed, setting completedAt timestamp
Implement 'todo remove <id>' command to delete a task, with confirmation prompt
Implement 'todo edit <id>' command to update title/description/priority of an existing task
Implement 'todo clear' command to remove all completed tasks (with confirmation)
Add input validation for all commands (e.g., invalid id, missing title) with clear error messages

phases.name: UX Polish
steps: Add colored, formatted console output for list command (e.g., green checkmark for completed, red for high priority)
Add helpful error messages and --help text for each command via Commander's built-in help system
Add a 'todo stats' command showing counts of total/completed/pending tasks
Handle edge cases: empty task list message, invalid/missing task ID, empty title input

phases.name: Testing
steps: Write unit tests for storage.js (load/save/init) using a temp/mock file path
Write unit tests for each command's core logic (add, list, done, remove, edit) by mocking storage functions
Write integration tests that invoke the CLI as a subprocess and check stdout output for key commands
Achieve reasonable coverage on task manipulation logic

phases.name: Packaging & Documentation
steps: Write README.md with installation instructions (npm install -g .), usage examples for every command, and screenshots/sample output
Add shebang line (#!/usr/bin/env node) to entry file and verify executable permissions
Test global installation locally via 'npm link' and verify 'todo' command works from any directory
Tag a v1.0.0 release in package.json

manual_checklist: Ensure Node.js 20+ is installed on the development/build machine
Run 'npm link' locally to test global CLI installation before publishing
Optionally publish package to npm registry (requires npm account and 'npm publish')
Decide and confirm the storage file location (default ~/.todo-cli/tasks.json) is acceptable for target OS/users

idea: a CLI todo app with local storage

plan.summary: A command-line interface application allowing users to add, list, complete, and delete tasks, persisting the entire task list to a local JSON file.

phases.name: Phase 1: Setup and Data Handling
steps: Initialize the project structure: create a main directory and a required task storage file (e.g., 'tasks.json') with an empty list `"tasks": []`.

phases.name: Phase 2: Core Functionality Implementation (CRUD)
steps: Develop a function to load the current task list from `tasks.json`. This function must handle `FileNotFoundError` by returning an empty list and creating the file if necessary.

phases.name: Phase 3: CLI Interface and Task Addition
steps: Implement the `add_task` function: This function reads the current tasks, accepts a task description via command-line argument, assigns a unique ID (integer counter), sets the initial status to 'pending', appends the new task dictionary to the list, and saves the updated list back to `tasks.json`.

phases.name: Phase 4: Listing and Viewing Tasks
steps: Implement the `list_tasks` command: This function reads all tasks, iterates through them, and prints a formatted output for each: [ID] - [Status] - [Description]. If no tasks exist, print a polite message.

phases.name: Phase 5: Completing and Deleting Tasks
steps: Implement the `complete_task` function: This function accepts a task ID. It must read tasks, find the task by ID, update its status to 'completed', and save the list. If the ID is invalid, it must print an error message.

phases.name: Phase 6: Task Deletion and CLI Polish
steps: Implement the `delete_task` function: This function accepts a task ID. It must read tasks, filter out the task with that ID, save the resulting shorter list, and provide confirmation messages.

phases.name: Phase 7: Aggregation and Testing
steps: Refactor all implemented functions into a cohesive main CLI entry point using Python's `argparse` module to handle subcommands (`todo add`, `todo list`, `todo done <id>`, `todo rm <id>`).

manual_checklist: Ensure the initial `tasks.json` file structure is correct and present in the root directory before running any code.
